summary: Kazu Uehara was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who completed graduate coursework at Kyushu University by 1992. He held posts as lecturer at the University of Miyazaki (~1961–1965) and professor at Seijo University (~1965–1995).

Kazuaki Komine worked in Japanology and Buddhist studies, earning degrees including a doctorate from Waseda University. He taught at Waseda Jitsugyo Gakko, Tokushima University, the National Institute of Japanese Literature, and served as professor at Rikkyo University (1995–2013).

Kazuaki Tanahashi is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Soichi Nakamura. He served as scholar in residence at the San Francisco Zen Center (1977–1984) and became a fellow of the World Academy of Art and Science.

Kazufumi Oki is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University. He taught Shindo Kusumoto and served as assistant professor (attested 1982–1988) and professor emeritus (attested 2006–2013) at Shuchiin University.

Kazuharu Mizuno is a geography and Tibetology scholar who studied at Nagoya University, Hokkaido University, and Tokyo Metropolitan University (DSc, ~1990). He became a professor in the Graduate School of Letters at Kyoto University around 2009.

A scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, Kazuhiko Yoshida studied at Sophia, Kyoto, Osaka, and Cornell universities under Jay Jasanoff and Teizo Iyanaga. He served as professor at Kyoto University (~2004–2021) and Nagoya City University (2021–2024).

Kazuhiro Kawasaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed doctoral studies at Koyasan University. He held positions at Koyasan University as a researcher (attested 2005) and specially appointed professor (attested 2026).
Kazuhiro Yamamoto specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Silpakorn University (attested 2009) under doctoral supervisors Samniang Leurmsai and Chirapat Prapandvidya.

Kazunobu Matsuda is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University under Shiro Matsumoto. He taught at Otani University (attested 1985–1989) and Bukkyo University (attested 1995–2007, 2009, 2022–2024), and belonged to Toho Kenkyukai.

Kazuo Hyodo specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and Otani University under Hajime Sakurabe, later serving as an assistant professor at Otani University (~1983–2014) and as a committee member for the Otani Society.

Kazuo Kano is a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology scholar educated at Kyoto University under Katsumi Mimaki and the University of Hamburg under Klaus-Dieter Mathes and David P. Jackson. He taught at Hamburg, Koyasan University (~2009–2017), and Komazawa University (~2017).

Kazuo Okabe is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the Institute for Zen Studies (1969) and Komazawa University (assistant professor 1973; professor 1979–2006).

Kazuo Osumi is a scholar of Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo. He was an assistant professor at Hokkaido University (1964) and a professor at Tokyo Woman's Christian University (1977–2001).
Kazuo Oyamada is a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tamagawa University and held a post at Rissho University.

Kazutoshi Ueda was a linguist and Japanologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and under Basil Hall Chamberlain and Georg von der Gabelentz. He taught at the University of Tokyo, Kokugakuin, and Kogakkan, and served in the House of Peers.

Kazuyoshi Hotta is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who pursued doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo. He served as director at the Tokyo University Buddhist Association (attested 2007) and term assistant professor at Otani University (attested 2015).

Kazuyoshi Kino was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who graduated from the University of Tokyo (1942–1948). He founded Shinnyokai and served as president of Hosen Gakuen College (1989) and vice-president of Shogen Junior College (1993).
Kazuyoshi Soma is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Meiji Yamada. He held a post as lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1987).
Keenan W. Cox is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who completed an MA at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn (attested 2014).

Kees W. Bolle studied religious studies and Indology at Leiden, Madras, and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade. He lectured at Brown University (~1961–1964) and was a professor of history at UCLA (~1969–1994).
